$comment: ROADMAP Phase 1A step 1 - the canonical combat-state definitions. Engine-neutral: the Unreal sandbox implements exactly this machine (Rule 22 / Decision 0002). One machine set for every player, mode and CPU fighter (Rule 5). Definitions only - no simulation code or engine implementation is claimed (Rule 18). Semantics: docs/phase1a/combat_state_definitions.md.

match_flow.$comment: Owned by the authoritative Match Controller. Segments mirror fight_event clock.segment. Decision assembly reads sealed judge cards inside the controller only; partial cards stay sealed through the immediate result flow (Rule 3).

states.description: Entrances, referee disclosure (Rule 16), fighter presentation. No combat resolution.
A round is live. The authoritative fight clock runs; all systems read it (Rule 9).
30 real-second break. Menu and statistics access do not pause the countdown (Rule 9).
A fighter is down. The universal knockdown-count clock runs, referee-synchronized (Rule 16).
Referee-initiated medical inspection under universal medical minimums (Rule 16). Eye and cut condition feed doctor confidence (Rule 14).
Result, quick menu, statistics. Official cards remain sealed during this immediate flow; optional archival reveal comes later (Rule 3).
Terminal. The authoritative event log is closed and becomes replay evidence (sandbox criteria E.19-E.21).

transitions.trigger_detail: entrance sequence complete; first bell
round clock reaches zero and the scheduled bout continues
30 real seconds elapse, or an in-match dual-consent skip (Rule 9)
a fighter_action machine enters knocked_down
rise accepted before ten plus mandatory referee look (universal minimums, Rule 16)
count reaches ten, or referee waves off during the count
referee pauses action for medical inspection
doctor confidence sufficient to continue
doctor stoppage
last scheduled round expires; decision assembled from sealed cards by the Match Controller only (Rule 3)
in-round stoppage: waved off, failure to intelligently defend, disqualification, or corner retirement at the bell
post-fight flow complete; log sealed as replay evidence

fighter_action.$comment: One per fighter, identical for human and CPU control (Rule 5). Action phases bind to move data: startup_frames, active_frames, recovery_frames from data/moves (Rule 22). CPU policies read only allowed_input_domains (Rule 3).

states.description: Uncommitted. Full action availability; the posture continuum governs locomotion in parallel.
Committed to a move; startup_frames from move data. Commitment is real: no cancel to idle after commit (Rule 13 explicit commitment). Interruptible by incoming contact.
states.notes: Startup interception is the first counter window (Rule 22: counterplay from the first punch).

states.description: Active window; active_frames from move data. Offensive categories resolve contact into the seven classes of data/contact_classes.json; evasion categories classify incoming punches as dodged; guard categories transition to guard_hold.
Post-action vulnerability; recovery_frames from move data, scaled by the commitment tier of the outcome. The deepest counter window.
states.notes: Rule 13: blocked < dodged < whiffed strictly increasing recovery and stamina consequence. Numerical ratios are tuning hypotheses.

states.description: Sustained guard after a guard move completes. Reduces clean damage without erasing consequence; absorbs into arms and guard structure over time (Rule 14).
states.notes: Passive blocking abuse becomes readable and counterable through guard fatigue, not hidden punishment (Rule 4).

states.description: Mutual tie-up entered through a successful clinch move. Referee tendencies govern permitted duration and inside work (Rule 16).
Reaction to landed contact. Magnitude scales with contact class, target region, and the struck fighter's chin_state, durability_state and composure_state (Rule 14). Tick-anchored duration.
Balance-compromised. Entered when balance crosses an authored threshold; visibly readable so spectators understand decisive exchanges (Rule 19).
On the canvas. The match_flow machine enters knockdown_count; the universal count clock is the only exit timer (Rule 16).
Attempting to beat the count. Success requires the count clock and the mandatory referee look.
In the corner during the break. Corner advice operates under Rule 6 bounds and never uses official scores.
Terminal for this fighter: ko, tko_referee_waveoff, tko_failure_to_intelligently_defend, tko_doctor, corner_retirement, or disqualification. Chin +100 resists longest but is never immune (Rule 14).
PROVISIONED (ROADMAP step 12). Motion-command Special (Rule 15): command entry cannot bypass stun, recovery, resource cost, range, tracking limits, startup, counterplay, or whiff punishment.
PROVISIONED (ROADMAP step 12). Full Crowd Bar choice, Ultimate branch. Powerful but counterable; never an automatic match end (Rule 11).
PROVISIONED (ROADMAP step 12). Full Crowd Bar choice, Trait branch. Exclusive with ultimate_execution per bar (Rule 12).

transitions.trigger_detail: human input or CPU decision selects a move from data/moves; CPU decisions emit cpu_decision records with cited observable evidence
startup_frames elapse
transitions.notes: punch_thrown for punch categories only; movement and defensive categories emit their outcome at resolution.

transitions.trigger_detail: active_frames elapse; contact resolves into exactly one of the seven contact classes for offensive categories
transitions.notes: Category-dependent: exactly one primary outcome event per action. A visible miss is never classified as a clean hit (Rule 13).

transitions.trigger_detail: recovery_frames elapse, scaled by contact_class_commitment_tier
guard-category moves settle into a held guard instead of recovery
guard dropped voluntarily
guard_integrity or arm condition fails under intelligent varied pressure; predictable single-action spam does not earn this (Rule 14)
clinch-category move succeeds at clinch range
referee separation per profile tendencies, or mutual release
a landed contact class (clean, solid, grazed, brushed) against this fighter; guard_impact instead when the guard absorbs it
transitions.notes: Movement into the punch may increase consequence; away may reduce it (Rule 14).

transitions.trigger_detail: follow-up contact during stun re-anchors and scales the stun window; no infinite-stun loop may result (Rule 4, sandbox F.25)
tick-anchored stun window ends
balance falls below authored threshold
balance recovers above threshold
further contact or failed weight transfer while staggered
observable evidence chain: force, placement, contact quality, movement, balance, awareness, accumulated condition, failed defense (explains links). Never a flat per-punch roll (Rule 14).
fighter attempts to rise; CPU intent uses count_observable and own_condition only
upright before ten with mandatory referee look passed (Rule 16 universal minimums)
not upright by ten, or referee judges the rise insufficient
count reaches ten with no accepted rise: ko
waved off, failure to intelligently defend, or disqualification, under universal medical and incapacitation minimums (Rule 16)
doctor stoppage driven by observable condition including side-specific eye damage (Rule 14 doctor confidence)
round clock reaches zero; the bell interrupts any standing action
break ends (Rule 9: 30 real seconds, menus do not pause it)
corner retires the fighter between rounds

PROVISIONED step 12: Specials resolve through the same commitment phases as every move
PROVISIONED step 12: full Crowd Bar spent on the Ultimate branch; the same bar can never also activate the trait (Rule 12)
PROVISIONED step 12: counterable resolution; never an automatic match end (Rule 11)

PROVISIONED step 12: trait window ends

posture_continuum.$comment: Rule 13: one continuous threat-responsive footwork model. These are modes of a continuum, not gating states - transition_delay_frames is zero by construction and the schema enforces it. Locomotion runs in parallel with fighter_action availability.can_move.

modes.description: Longer responsive strides at safe distance.
Compressed believable steps inside threatening range (threat-responsive stride compression).
modes.notes: Compression follows observable threat, not a mode toggle.

modes.description: Planted feet: full power transfer available; visible weight transfer (Rule 13).
Planted pivots and angle changes; the believable mechanism for stance switching (Rule 15).

stance.switch_mechanism: Stance changes emerge through steps, pivots, pullbacks and angle changes - never a slow artificial transition (Rule 15). Emits stance_change. Non-ambidextrous fighters operate under authored familiarity penalties outside their stated stance; ambidextrous fighters have none, but keep ordinary balance, commitment and positioning consequences.
stance.notes: Stance is a dimension of the fighter, not a blocking state. Penalties are data-driven from fighter attributes (Rule 10 families).

invariants.statement: No state guard or transition may read official_scorecards or sealed_events. Fighter, CPU, referee, corner, commentary, crowd, difficulty, live-replay and advice systems form estimates only from observable events with explicit confidence.
Recovery and stamina consequence strictly increase across blocked, dodged, whiffed outcomes; move_recovery scales by contact_class_commitment_tier.
Every offensive commitment exposes counter vulnerability: startup interception, active trade, and a counter-open recovery.
Transitions into knocked_down require condition_threshold or incoming_contact evidence chains with explains links; a flat per-punch knockout roll does not exist.
Posture modes are a continuum: transition_delay_frames is constant zero; no ice skating, magnetic range correction, invisible lunges, or artificial movement-mode transition delays.
Every duration and trigger is tick-anchored; wall-clock trigger kinds do not exist; the same seed and authoritative initial state reproduce a byte-identical event log.
chin_state scales resistance in hit_stun and knockdown thresholds; Chin +100 is maximum authored resistance, never immunity, and rare early stoppages remain possible on observable evidence.
invariants.enforced_by: data statement; promoted to a simulation test at ROADMAP step 8

invariants.statement: One full Crowd Bar activates ultimate_execution or full_crowd_trait_active, never both. Provisioned until ROADMAP steps 11-12.
Referee-triggered transitions may hold, separate, instruct or stop; they never alter damage, stamina, collision classification, Crowd gain, attributes, input responsiveness or judging criteria.
Exactly one machine set exists for every player, mode, difficulty and CPU fighter. Beginner, child or tiered variants are prohibited.
